decisions.title: Ratify the updater-safety workstream (eight updater-script changes plus sps2/tests/test_updater_safety.py) as an authorized safety-hardening workstream
decisions.decision: The User's Round 16 decision message, received 2026-10-16, is transcribed verbatim between the BEGIN/END markers in the evidence array below. Its line 'UPDATER-SAFETY WORKSTREAM: RATIFY' resolves audit finding G-1 (reports/SPS2-ROUND15-READ-ONLY-VERIFICATION-20261016-175720.md, §9/§10 finding 1): the eight modified tracked updater files (get-sps.ps1, get-sps.sh, scripts/bootstrap-sps.sh, scripts/sps-update.sh, scripts/update-sps.ps1, skills/sps/scripts/bootstrap-sps.sh, skills/sps/scripts/sps-update.sh, skills/sps/scripts/update-sps.ps1) and the untracked sps2/tests/test_updater_safety.py are hereby ratified as a safety-hardening workstream. Ratification covers the changes as they exist in the working tree at HEAD c49f385 — removal of bootstrap auto-update execution, removal of git reset --hard / rm -rf / Remove-Item -Recurse -Force destructive fallbacks, addition of dirty-worktree refusal and non-git-destination refusal, and the accompanying behavioral test module. This ratification authorizes the changes to stand; it does NOT authorize commit or push (the message says so explicitly, and COMMIT/PUSH: NOT AUTHORIZED is restated as its own line).
decisions.reason: The Round 15 audit verified the changes are genuine safety hardening with behavioral test coverage, but found no governance record authorizing them. The User has now supplied that authorization. Recording it closes the governance gap without granting any publication or git action.

decisions.title: Authorize inventory digest regeneration: write only the two Round 15-verified digest values into P10-SECTION-INVENTORY.json provenance
decisions.decision: The User's Round 16 decision line 'INVENTORY DIGEST REGENERATION: AUTHORIZE' authorizes writing exactly two values into sps2/requirements/P10-SECTION-INVENTORY.json: provenance.cms_state_digest = sha256:b35f7aba68eca4e7c9b688ae979891330f2f3d08c2b4250ce855c55943f7e38e and provenance.p8_contract_digest = sha256:ee6bb68f04f0eb468f0fd6eafaaea0b68639b88199e207c7a76ef57e10bbf217. Both values were independently recomputed in the Round 15 read-only audit (reports/SPS2-ROUND15-READ-ONLY-VERIFICATION-20261016-175720.md §7) by a from-scratch reimplementation of the DEC-7112 canonical scheme, cross-checked against the gate's own helper, and were recomputed a second time immediately before this write with identical results. No other inventory field is changed by this authorization: inventory_state, user_approval, section states, and every other key remain byte-identical. This authorization does NOT publish content and does NOT set user_approval (both explicitly withheld by the same message). This decision supersedes, for these two values only, the blanket 'writing inventory digest values is not approved' clause recorded at the time of the six-semantics adoption (DEC-7112's explicitly_not_approved_by_this_record list, entry 2).
decisions.reason: The cms-state-digest and p8-contract-digest controls fail closed on null. The values are now independently verified; writing them lifts two of the gate's six honest failures and converts those controls from fail-closed placeholders into real, recomputable integrity claims over the CMS state and ContentType contract.
